description: Wire vectors of the TxnOffsetCommit API (key 28, v0 to v6), replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: TxnOffsetCommit request v0, the only request of the transaction protocol that goes to the **group** coordinator: the offset 2 of `t8-vectors`-0 is committed for the group `t8-vectors-group` inside the transaction of `t8-vectors-txn`. There is no generation id and no member id in it - the producer is not a member of the group, and the producer epoch is what fences it instead.

The answer of the group coordinator: one entry per requested partition, the error code 0 for an offset that was written into `__consumer_offsets` as a transactional record. It stays invisible to an OffsetFetch of the group until the transaction is committed.
TxnOffsetCommit request v1, the frame of version 0 with the api version Kafka 2.0 added: one offset with its metadata, committed inside the transaction rather than with an OffsetCommit.
TxnOffsetCommit response v1: the error code 0 of the partition whose offset the coordinator wrote.

TxnOffsetCommit request v2, the first frame of this api that Kafka really changed: every partition carries the `committed_leader_epoch` of KIP-320 between the offset and the metadata - the epoch 0 of a partition whose leader was never re-elected.
TxnOffsetCommit response v2: the frame of version 0, and the error code 0 of the partition whose offset the group coordinator wrote with that epoch.

TxnOffsetCommit request v3 (KIP-447), the first flexible version of the api: the `generation_id`, the `member_id` and the `group_instance_id` the version added name the consumer whose offsets the transaction commits, and the coordinator refuses the commit of a member that has been rebalanced away.
TxnOffsetCommit answer v3: the error code 0 of the one partition, in the compact encoding.
TxnOffsetCommit answer v3 to a commit whose `generation_id` is not the one the group is in: the error code 22 (IllegalGeneration) per partition, which is what KIP-447 added the three fields for.
TxnOffsetCommit answer v3 to a commit with a `member_id` the group does not have: the error code 25 (UnknownMemberId) per partition.

TxnOffsetCommit request v4 (Kafka 3.8, KIP-890): the version 3 frame of KIP-447 field for field - the generation -1 and the empty member id of a producer that is not a member of the group, a null `group_instance_id`, and the offset 42 of `t4-38-vectors-0` with the leader epoch -1 and a null metadata. "Version 4 adds support for new error code TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890)" is all the version says (`TxnOffsetCommitRequest.json` @ 3.8.1). This frame goes to the **group** coordinator, not to the transaction coordinator.
TxnOffsetCommit answer v4: the per-partition code 0 of the group coordinator, which wrote the offset as a transactional record that stays invisible until the COMMIT marker.
The same version 4 with the membership of KIP-447 filled in: the generation 99 and the member id `t4-38-no-such-member` of a group that has no member at all.

The refusal: **25** `UnknownMemberId` per partition, one of the three codes the version 3 added, at the version 4 unchanged - the member id is checked before the generation, so the 22 of an illegal generation needs a member the group really holds.

TxnOffsetCommit request v4 of a transaction that holds a partition of `t4-38-vectors` but **not** the `__consumer_offsets` partition of `t4-38-vectors-group`, because no AddOffsetsToTxn preceded it. The group coordinator verifies that partition against the transaction coordinator before it writes the offset - the partition verification of KIP-890 part 1, `transaction.partition.verification.enable` - and this is the one client-facing frame of the wave whose refusal the version really changes.

The **120** `TransactionAbortable` per partition, the code Kafka 3.8 declared, answered to a client because its version says it understands it: `GroupCoordinator.handleTxnCommitOffsets` @ 3.9.2 chooses `transactionSupportedOperation = if (apiVersion >= 4) genericError else defaultError`, and `AddPartitionsToTxnManager` passes the code through instead of folding it into the 48.

The very same commit at the **version 3**, three bytes longer only because the transactional id of the second transaction is: the frames are otherwise identical, and the version field is what decides the answer.

The **48** `InvalidTxnState` a version 3 is answered for the same situation - `AddPartitionsToTxnManager` @ 3.9.2 maps the 120 back "for backward compatibility with clients" whose version does not promise to understand it. The two frames next to each other are the whole content of KIP-890 part 2 on this node.

TxnOffsetCommit request v4 on the 4.3.1 node, which finalizes `transaction.version` 2: the producer `t4-40-vectors-tx` has just been initialized and commits the offset 7 of `t4-40-vectors-0` for `t4-40-vectors-group` without an AddOffsetsToTxn in front of it - a transaction of the protocol v2 that sends the version of the protocol v1. The group coordinator only verifies the `__consumer_offsets` partition of the group at this version (the partition verification of KIP-890 part 1).

The **120** `TransactionAbortable` per partition: the verification of KIP-890 part 1 reporting a partition the transaction does not hold, on a node that has the feature exactly as on the 3.9.2 node that did not. `txnOffsetCommitRequestVersionToTransactionSupportedOperation` @ 4.0.0 maps the version 4 to `genericErrorSupported`, which verifies and does not enrol.

TxnOffsetCommit request v5 (Kafka 4.0, KIP-890 part 2): the very same commit a moment later, byte for byte the frame above but for the version field and the correlation id. "Version 5 is the same as version 4" (`TxnOffsetCommitRequest.json` @ 4.0.0) - and it is the switch of the protocol v2: a version above 4 is `addPartition`, the group coordinator enrols the offsets partition into the transaction itself.

TxnOffsetCommit answer v5: the code **0** for the commit the version 4 was refused the 120 for. The offsets partition is now part of the transaction, which this request has started - no AddOffsetsToTxn and no AddPartitionsToTxn went to the transaction coordinator at all.

TxnOffsetCommit request v6 (Kafka 4.4, KIP-1319) of the producer `t4-44-vectors-tx` - producer id 1000, epoch 0, right after its InitProducerId and without any AddOffsetsToTxn - for the group `t4-44-vectors-group` without a membership: the generation -1, the empty member id, the null instance id, and one topic entry that names `t4-44-vectors` by its **topic id**, the 16 raw bytes of the uuid in place of the compact string of the name, with the offset 7, the leader epoch -1 and the null metadata of partition 0.

The answer names the topic by the same id and nothing else, the partition with the code **0**. Like the version 5 the version 6 is `addPartition`: the group coordinator enrolled the `__consumer_offsets` partition of the group into the transaction this request started, and the EndTxn v5 that commits it makes the offset 7 visible to an OffsetFetch.
The same producer inside the same transaction, the topic entry naming an id the node does not know - `8f3c2a5e0b6d4e1f9a7c3b2d1e0f4a5b`, made up for the frame - with the offset 8.

The **100** `UNKNOWN_TOPIC_ID` on the partition, the id echoed back: `KafkaApis.handleTxnOffsetCommitRequest` @ 4.4.0 resolves the ids through the metadata cache of the node before it authorizes the topics and answers an id it can not resolve itself, without asking the group coordinator.

A commit for the group `t4-44-vectors-no-such-group`, which does not exist, in the name of a member of it - the generation 5 and the member id `t4-44-no-such-member` - under the epoch 1 the commit of the first transaction bumped the producer to.

The **69** `GROUP_ID_NOT_FOUND`: from the version 6 on `OffsetMetadataManager.validateTransactionalOffsetCommit` @ 4.4.0 lets the `GroupIdNotFoundException` through (`TxnOffsetCommitRequest.supportsGroupIdNotFoundError`). The generation -1 would have created a simple group instead.
The same commit at the version 5, which names the topic.
The **22** `ILLEGAL_GENERATION`: the legacy mapping of an unknown group that every version below 6 keeps.

A commit in the name of the member of the KIP-848 group `t4-44-vectors-848` that joined it with a ConsumerGroupHeartbeat and holds the member epoch 2, with the epoch **3** - one above it - in the field `generation_id_or_member_epoch`, the `generationId` of this client.

The **113** `STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH`: `ConsumerGroup.validateOffsetCommit` @ 4.4.0 refuses an epoch above the one the member holds, and the version 6 lets the code through (`supportsStaleMemberEpochError`).
The same commit with the epoch 3 at the version 5.
The **22** `ILLEGAL_GENERATION`, the code a version below 6 is answered for the stale member epoch.
The same commit with the member epoch 2 the coordinator holds for the member.
The code **0**: the member epoch of a KIP-848 member stands where a classic member writes its generation. The producer aborted the transaction afterwards.
